text: Before trusting a gap between two versions, measure how much one version moves by itself: two soups of the same aadha arm differed by 13 to 16 lines on the large sets, and one seed moved rai's count by about thirty answers.

Put the same test to a hosted model before building: on 603 sentences I had marked, Haiku and Sonnet matched or beat aadha on the good noise, and aadha was ahead on only one boundary, abstract nonsense.
Compare with a parser or a rule first: on plain notings a sentence parser alone got 162 of 178 acts where RAM got 178.
Compare with a few lines of plain code: Beam's thread model picked the same as plain code 88% to 100% of the time, so the model added nothing.

Before training, set the weights at full strength and measure how far the choices can move what they are meant to change: the maze maker could move the walk only from 41 to 32 key presses, so I scrapped it.

If a model wrote the test rows, a high score says little. Every test answer for rai was written in Claude Code, and the argument models had no human test set; measure on people's own writing before trusting a figure.

Time it on the Pi itself: the uncut audio encoder took 2,070 ms a window on a Pi 5, the encoder cut to two seconds 65 ms on a Mac mini. The microphone picks up the fan, so fit the model with the fan running.
The only figure is a published one on isolated English commands; words inside running speech, and Hindi or Hinglish, are not measured.
Count what always giving the commonest answer scores: kahen got 108 of 179, and always answering 'the point' got 107.
